title: Securities Trading Policy
date_effective: the date of the Company's admission to the Official List of ASX

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of any company in the Group. Subject to Prohibited Period restrictions, prior written approval and subsequent notification for all Trading, the margin loan/security approval regime, and the section 3.8 hedging/derivatives restriction on unvested Company Securities. Designated Officer for a Director is the Chair (or the CEO if the Director is the Chair).

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: The CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, General Counsel, employees involved in preparing the Group's monthly financial reports, direct reports to those positions, and any employee nominated by the Board and notified accordingly. Subject to the identical Prohibited Period, approval, notification, margin loan and hedging regime as Directors. Designated Officer for a Restricted Employee is the Company Secretary (or the CEO if the Restricted Employee is the Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any full or part time employee of any Group member. Subject only to the general insider trading prohibition and the universal short-term trading ban; not subject to Prohibited Periods, the approval/notification regime, the margin loan approval requirement, or the section 3.8 hedging restriction, none of which extend beyond Directors and Restricted Employees.

exceptions.evidence: (Severe financial hardship): a pressing financial commitment that can only be satisfied by selling the relevant Company Securities

(Court order): a requirement to Trade in Company Securities as a result of: a court order; court enforceable undertakings (eg as part of a bona fide family settlement); or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement
(Other circumstances): any other circumstances considered exceptional by the Designated Officer

(Involuntary disposals caused by margin lender) An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement.

An investment in, or Trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

Where the Director or Restricted Employee is a trustee or a director of a corporate trustee, Trading in Company Securities by that trust provided the Director or Restricted Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or directors or by the investment managers independently of the Director or Restricted Employee.
(Accepting a takeover offer) Undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer, or participation in a scheme of arrangement.

(Exercise of options or rights) The exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme. This exception applies to options and rights granted under an employee incentive scheme before this Policy takes effect.

The exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Prohibited Period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long Prohibited Period or the entity has had a number of consecutive Prohibited Periods and the Director or Restricted Employee could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.

exemption_authority: The Designated Officer (Chair for a Director, CEO for the Chair, Company Secretary for a Restricted Employee, CEO for the Company Secretary, or another Board-appointed officer) may determine that Exceptional Circumstances apply and grant prior written approval to Trade during a Prohibited Period; the discretion is exercised 'with caution' and may be refused without reasons. No broader Board-level general waiver power beyond this is stated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative has the meaning in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, cash settled swaps, caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only policy in this batch to expressly name 'collars' as a covered instrument, removing definitional doubt that a funded equity collar with a bank is a Derivative and hence a Security requiring ordinary Trade approval once vested, not an outright-banned instrument.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not use, or allow to be used, any Derivatives or other products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The absolute hedging/derivatives ban applies only to unvested Company Securities; once shares vest, a collar is not banned at all and is treated as ordinary Trading requiring standard prior written approval, materially more favourable than a blanket hedging ban regardless of vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Director or Restricted Employee may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited, only subject to Designated Officer approval, ongoing LVR/drawdown disclosure, and at least annual reporting of amount drawn and securities covered.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out with residual approval tension
bespoke_clauses.clause: An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement [is permitted during a Prohibited Period]. (Please note that the Policy requirements with respect to prior written approval and subsequent notification continue to apply to Trading under one of these exceptions.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, but the Policy states prior-approval and notification duties technically continue to apply even to this exception, a practical tension (an involuntary sale cannot easily obtain prior approval) worth clarifying with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A tax liability relating to Securities received under an employee incentive scheme would also not normally constitute severe financial hardship or otherwise be considered an exceptional circumstance for the purpose of obtaining proper written approval to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Prohibited Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or sale timed specifically to fund tax due on vesting of incentive securities cannot rely on the Exceptional Circumstances gateway to trade inside a Prohibited Period; timing must fall within an open window instead.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval for the Trading will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (or its unwind) must be priced and executed within 7 days of Designated Officer approval or the approval lapses and must be sought again.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is achievable for both Directors and Restricted Employees under this policy, and is one of the more favourable of its kind: the Schedule expressly defines 'Derivative' to include 'collars', and section 3.8's hedging/derivatives ban applies only to unvested Company Securities, so a collar over vested shares is simply an ordinary Trade requiring prior written approval from the Designated Officer (the Chair for a Director, the Company Secretary for a Restricted Employee), outside a Prohibited Period, with approval valid for only 7 days and subsequent notification to the Company Secretary within two business days. The loan leg is separately and expressly permitted: entering a margin loan or similar funding arrangement, or granting lenders any rights over the collared shares, requires only the Designated Officer's prior written approval plus ongoing disclosure of material changes (e.g. LVR movements) and at least annual reporting of the amount drawn and securities covered, with no outright secured-financing ban. A lender's forced sale on enforcement of the loan is excluded from the Prohibited Period restriction, though the Policy's own wording states that prior-approval and notification duties technically continue to apply to that exception, a tension worth clarifying with the Company Secretary. One important limitation: a tax liability arising from vesting of incentive securities is expressly stated not normally to constitute an Exceptional Circumstance, so a collar or sale timed to fund such a tax liability cannot rely on that gateway to trade inside a Prohibited Period.
